title: Delegated shedder proxy with weighted burst rejoin and soft-failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The global admission limiter has proven effective at preventing downstream overload, but outages and latency spikes in the limiter control plane can cause widespread 5xxs or unpredictable token drops. Recent incidents show two classes of pain: (1) short, high-concurrency bursts where tenants get unfairly serialized and starved by a single hot-path limiter node; (2) limiter control-plane partial outages where clients see sudden hard rejects with no graceful rejoin path.

Goals:
- Provide a proxy-level delegated shedder that can absorb bursts locally and smoothly rejoin to global quota, reducing hard rejects during transient limiter unavailability.
- Ensure per-tenant weighted fairness during burst absorption so high-priority customers are not starved by noisy tenants.
- Define operational runbook and telemetry to surface progressive degradation before SLO burn.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Reduce hard 429/503 spikes during limiter control-plane latency events by at least 75% in canary region.
- Maintain SLOs (p99 latency and availability) for P0 tenants within 5% of baseline under simulated burst tests.
- No increase in token over-consumption beyond safe slack (max 8% deviation) after rejoin.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Delegated Shedder Proxy: lightweight admission layer colocated with edge proxies. It implements a local soft-credits reservoir per tenant derived from downstream quota leases. On admission-plane degradation it can temporarily grant local credits to smooth bursts.
2) Weighted Burst Fairshare: reservoir refill rates and temporary credits are weighted by tenant priority, recent usage signal, and configured SLA tiers. We implement a two-stage weighting: long-term entitlement (weekly quota proportion) and short-term priority multiplier.
3) Lease Rejoin Protocol: when control-plane leases return, the proxy performs an epochal reconciliation: it announces a short rejoin window, pushes back excess optimistic consumption via delayed penalties (token debt) and throttles catch-up requests rather than immediate hard rejection.
4) Circuit-breaker Integration: proxies have a local circuit that trips into soft-fail (serve from reservoir + degrade non-critical routes) when controller heartbeats missing > 500ms for 3s. Full hard-fail occurs only after 30s without reconciliation.
5) Telemetry: emit metrics for reservoir size, optimistic-consumed, debt, rejoin-events, per-tenant fairness score. Add tracing for rejoin negotiations.

Trade-offs and safeguards:
- Risk: optimistic credits could allow short-term over-consumption of GPUs. Mitigation: strict upper-bound on reservoir size (configurable, default 5% of tenant committed quota), and global reconciliation that enforces debt throttling.
- Complexity: lease rejoin protocol adds state and edge logic. Mitigation: keep proxy state ephemeral and persist only reconciled checkpoints to central store.

Operational runbook (summary):
- Detect: alert when reservoir exhaustion rate > 30% or rejoin-events > 5m windows, plus SLO burn.
- Triage: if controller heartbeat latency > 250ms, flip proxies to soft-fail (automated).
- Remediation: during long controller outage, increase reservoir smoothing parameter for top-tier tenants, and enable limited emergency global credits if SLA indicates.
- Postmortem: reconcile debt ledger, apply compensation rate-limits for offending tenants, and update thresholds.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement read-only proxy with synthetic reservoir simulator, deploy to us-west-2 edge cluster, run SLO-preserving canary tests.
- Phase 1 (pilot): enable delegated shedder in write mode for 5 internal tenants + 3 opt-in customers; monitor debt/backpressure and fairness metrics for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (ramp): expand to all regions with gradual global weighting tuning and default policies.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should debt be stored centrally or sharded per-region? (tradeoff: central consistency vs. regional availability).
- Default reservoir size: 2% vs 5% of committed quota? (we propose 5% for initial pilot).
- Interaction with Dedicated capacity tenants that have strict isolation: add opt-out flag per tenant.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Delegated+Shedder+Proxy+Design
- Simulation harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/limiter-sims/pulls/128
- Benchmark dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/limiter/burst-fairshare-canary

Notes: This ticket focuses on engineering design, telemetry, and runbook. Follow-up tickets will cover tenant opt-outs, Dedicated integration, and console UX for debt visibility.
